newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS appeals $8.0 mln ADM settlement.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS appeals $8.0 mln ADM settlement.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS), which holds 2.8 million shares of Archer Daniels Midland Co, said Thursday it appealed an $8 million lawsuit settlement made by ADM.

CalPERS said it and the Florida Retirement System Trust Fund oppose the $8.0 million settlement of shareholder lawsuits as inadequate. It also charged that the corporate governance principles to be adopted by ADM under the settlement are only "minor modifications."

The settlement, presented to shareholders in early June and recently approved in an Urbana, Ill., federal court, stems from a derivative lawsuit against directors of ADM for their alleged role in an antitrust suit brought against the company by the U.S. Department of Justice.
The shareholder suits alleged that certain current and former ADM directors did not prevent the activities that led to ADM's 1996 guilty plea to price-fixing violations.

"This deal does not even come close to recovering the estimated $190 million loss suffered by the company and its shareholders," William Crist, president of the CalPERS Board of Administration, said in a statement.
A CalPERS spokesman could not quantify the $190 million loss claim.
Last year, ADM paid $100 million in criminal fines after pleading guilty to charges of fixing the prices of lysine, a feed additive, and citric acid, an additive used in foods and other products.
The Decatur, Ill.-based agribusiness giant also agreed to a $35 million settlement of a citric acid civil price-fixing suit and to a $25 million settlement of a lysine civil case.
Other legal actions, including a civil case brought by high fructose corn syrup buyers, are pending.
CalPERS said it objected to the settlement which, it claimed, would earmark 49 percent -- or nearly $4 million -- in fees for the plaintiff's attorneys.

CalPERS said it also opposes corporate governance measures included in the settlement. Institutional shareholders have pressed for governance reforms at ADM in the wake of the antitrust investigation, including a board dominated by outside directors with no professional or personal ties to the company or its chairman, Dwayne Andreas.
ADM did not respond to a request for reaction to CalPERS' appeal of the settlement.
